Not worth the time, effort or money. Better options all across Hanoi
Sep 2026 • Couples
Bleak experience and they’re trading on that past visit from Obama and Bourdain but standards must have slipped a long way.

Walk in and get blank stares from the people on the ground floor. Ask if they have space and they give a non-committal, vague gesture to the stairs. Take a seat in the first and second floor and you’ll sit there like a fool because they’re not serviced it seems. Head up to the 3rd floor and you’ll find it packed but the owners and staff won’t make eye contact or help in any way, so take a seat and sit anywhere.

When we sat down there were two unattended plates of bun (vermicelli noodles) alone, no idea how long they’d been there. We told the guy working there when we ordered, he walked off in the middle of my wife asking a question about the food, and obviously couldn’t care less, expecting us to eat the old food.

The leaves for the bun cha arrived and we had to argue with the older lady that works there to swap the unknown-age noodles for fresh food, she was obviously and noisily unhappy about not palming off the old garbage onto us, very reluctantly swapping them for new bowls. By the time the pork soup arrived, the noodles were cold, and the soup and meat was already lukewarm. Expecting something delicious due to the reputation, what we got was an underwhelming experience. The food isn’t bad, but it’s nothing special and I’ve had way better bun cha from dozens of street vendors and restaurants in the U.K., USA, Canada, and mainland Western Europe. So overall a total disappointment and I would NOT eat here again or recommend anyone else wastes their time and money doing so.

On the subject of money, check your bill because they were liberal with what they tried to charge upon exit, deciding to take their tip and additional for “something” they felt entitled to so had to be challenged on the total.

As far as the setting - it’s clean for a Hanoi old/french quarter eatery but it would fail a health inspection by any legitimate agency - liquid and solid food and old tissue all over the floor with nobody cleaning up despite not being that busy, most surfaces were dirty, tables left uncleared and uncleaned for long periods of times while the staff looked on bored but idle.

One to avoid, unless you really want to say you ate where Obama did.

The Famous Bún Chả Spot of Barack Obama and Anthony Bourdain
Jul 2026 • Couples
This was my second time dining here, although I never got around to reviewing my first visit three years ago. I came back because of Barack Obama and Anthony Bourdain, two people I truly admire.

We ordered the bún chả and the fried crab rolls. The bún chả was clean, flavorful, and I especially loved the grilled pork patties. While I’ve had even better bún chả from local street vendors in Hanoi, this one is still worth trying. The fried crab rolls were crispy, savory, and absolutely delicious.

The prices are affordable and the experience is worth it. We arrived around 12:45 PM, and although there was still a small crowd and a short waitlist, we were seated within five minutes. The restaurant has three floors, so the line moves quickly. Definitely a must visit when in Hanoi.

Solid shrine with food as a side note
Jun 2026 • Couples
Bun Cha is a specialty in Hanoi that you can certainly try at Bun Cha Huong Lien without major financial damage, but we all actually come for THAT table: blue stools under glass on the second floor, where Obama enjoyed the house specialty. As soon as you enter the restaurant, it becomes clear what this is about; photos of Obama hang everywhere, the menu lists an Obama combo for very little money, the atmosphere is, let's say: rustic. It is by no means particularly clean, the broth is lukewarm and cold after the first portion of noodles, the staff is very efficiently focused on high turnover. You can do it - and check it off as part of the sightseeing, not the culinary experience.

It is deceptively large inside, if you can't see a table at first, just go up another floor and try there!

Absolutely Delicious!
Feb 2026 • Couples
We had this restaurant as a definite on our list while visiting Hanoi simply because President O'Bama had eaten there. We simply ordered the O'Bama special which was bun cha and a fried seafood roll, and both were absolutely delicious. The bun cha broth had a pleasant sweetness and good quality small pork patties that appeared to have been grilled. I do not like fried foods, but enjoyed the quality taste of the seafood roll so no regrets on including that. Our tour guide warned us not to eat the lettuce because it is washed in local water so we simply asked them not to bring it since we had carefully avoided all non-bottled water all over SE Asia. We are very glad we ate here and suggest you keep on walking up in search of a table because we found one on the third level and it appeared there was also a fourth.
